source.notes: Assessed from the criterion text in WCAG 2.2 and the techniques it lists as failures, the W3C ACT rules listed for the criterion, and the rules this package implements. 'fully': every failure condition can be decided mechanically; 'partly': some conditions can, the rest need a person; 'not': it needs human judgement or running behaviour a static check cannot see.

criteria.basis: Whether an image, input, object or SVG has a text alternative or name is mechanical; whether the text serves the same purpose is judgement.
Whether an alternative or track exists is mechanical; whether it is equivalent is judgement.
Whether a captions track exists is mechanical; whether it is accurate and synchronised is judgement.
Whether a description track or media alternative exists is mechanical; whether it conveys the visual content is judgement.
Live captions can only be judged by watching a live event.
Whether a description track or alternative exists is mechanical; its adequacy is judgement.
A sign-language video cannot be recognised mechanically.
Whether extended description is needed and sufficient is judgement.
Whether a transcript or alternative is linked is mechanical; its completeness is judgement.
Live audio can only be judged by listening to a live event.
Markup that breaks structure (lists, tables, required ARIA parents and children, fake headings) is detectable; whether visual structure is also in the markup is judgement.
Whether the reading order is meaningful is judgement; a layout comparison only finds candidates.
Instructions that rely on shape, size or location are found by reading them.
CSS orientation locks are detectable; locks made by script are invisible to a static check.
Invalid autocomplete tokens are detectable; whether a field's purpose matches its token is judgement.
Whether a component's purpose is programmatically identified needs judgement about purpose.
Links distinguished only by colour inside text are detectable; other uses of colour to convey meaning are judgement.
Autoplaying media markup is detectable; audio started by script is invisible.
Contrast is exact where the foreground and a solid background are known; images, gradients and overlaps need rendered facts or review.
Markup that blocks zoom is detectable; whether content survives 200% zoom needs rendering.
Recognising text rendered as an image, and whether it is essential, is judgement.
As 1.4.3, with the higher thresholds.
Background audio levels need listening.
Computed line height, width, alignment and spacing are measurable; colour selection and the reading experience are judgement.
As 1.4.5, without the exceptions.
Overflow and clipping at 320 CSS pixels are measurable from a layout at that viewport; whether lost content matters is judgement.
Contrast of boundaries and graphics is measurable where colours are known; which parts are needed to identify a component is judgement.
Inline declarations that stop text spacing overrides are detectable; whether content survives the overrides needs rendering.
Content revealed on hover or focus is usually script-driven; whether it is dismissible, hoverable and persistent needs interaction.
Scrollable regions and frames a keyboard cannot reach are detectable; handlers added by script are invisible.
A keyboard trap shows only while tabbing through a running page.
Single-key shortcuts are installed by script.
Meta refresh time limits are detectable; timers in script are invisible.
Blinking and scrolling markup is detectable; other moving content needs judgement and timing.
Whether time limits are essential is judgement.
Automatic page refresh is detectable; other interruptions come from script.
Session expiry is server behaviour.
Whether users are warned about data loss is judgement of content.
Flash analysis needs the rendered frames of the content.
Flash analysis needs the rendered frames of the content.
Motion triggered by interaction is script-driven.
Skip links and landmarks are detectable; whether they bypass the right blocks is judgement.
A missing or empty title is detectable; whether it describes the page is judgement.
Positive tabindex and focusable elements without a role are detectable; whether the order is meaningful is judgement.
Links without a name are detectable; whether the name and context state the purpose is judgement.
Whether a site offers more than one way to find pages is a property of the whole site.
Empty headings and labels are detectable; whether they describe their content is judgement.
Rules that remove the focus outline are detectable under a focus context; whether another indicator is visible needs rendering.
Whether a page tells the user where they are is judgement of the whole site.
Identical link names with different targets are detectable; whether a name alone states the purpose is judgement.
Whether sections need headings is judgement.
Needs layout and paint order to know what covers the focused element; mechanical with rendered facts.
As 2.4.11, with the stricter condition.
Indicator size and contrast are measurable with rendered facts; whether a custom indicator is distinguishable is judgement.
Multipoint and path gestures are handled by script.
Pointer event handling is script behaviour.
Comparing visible label text with the accessible name is mechanical for text labels; labels made of images are judgement.
Motion actuation is script behaviour.
Target size is measurable with rendered facts; the exceptions are judgement.
Input mechanisms are script behaviour.
Dragging interactions are script behaviour.
Target size and spacing are measurable; the exceptions (inline, equivalent control, essential) are judgement.
A missing or malformed lang is detectable; whether it is the right language needs language identification.
Malformed lang on parts is detectable; whether passages are in the declared language needs language identification.
Unusual words and their definitions are judgement.
Abbreviations and their expansions are judgement.
Reading level is judgement.
Ambiguous pronunciation is judgement.
Context changes on focus come from script.
Forms without a submit control are detectable; changes of context on input come from script.
Consistency is a property of several pages.
Consistency is a property of several pages.
Automatic refresh is detectable; other changes of context come from script.
Consistency of help is a property of several pages.
Invalid-state and error-message association markup is detectable; whether an error is identified in text depends on runtime validation.
Controls without labels are detectable; whether labels and instructions are sufficient is judgement.
Error suggestions are runtime content.
Whether a page is legal or financial, and its safeguards, are judgement.
Whether help is available is judgement.
Submission safeguards are runtime behaviour.
Redundant entry spans steps of a process.
Missing autocomplete on authentication fields is detectable; script blocking of paste is invisible and the alternatives are judgement.
Duplicate ids and malformed nesting are decided by the parser and the document; the criterion is obsolete from WCAG 2.2.
Roles, names and states in markup and ARIA are decided mechanically; values changed by script are invisible.
Status messages are announced at runtime; markup alone cannot show that a message appears.
